The appellants were brought to trial on a charge of murder.
The trial court, on a consideration of the evidence, convicted both the accused for the offence punishable under Section 302 of the IPC

The prosecution relied primarily on the evidence of PW-6 Marjon Suklabaidhya, who was projected as an eye witness to what had happened on the fateful day, PW-1 Panchami Suklabaidya aforesaid, PW-2 the Executive Magistrate Manash Das, who held an inquest on the dead body and had noticed a huge cut injury on the person of the deceased, Radhu Paul PW-4 who stated that he had seen both the accused involved in an animated discussion in front of his shop and when he had gone close to them they had changed the topic and had started discussing some business matter and that after a short while a girl had come out and raised a hue and cry and told Mission Suklabaidhya that his wife had died of burn injuries, Nioti Rani PW-6, the mother of the deceased, who deposed to the illicit relationship of her son-in-law and PW-1, and PW-7 the doctor, Khairuz Zaman Choudhary, who had carried out the post-mortem examination and had found very severe cut injuries on the stomach which indicated that the foetus had been removed.

trial_court_outcome.value: Convicted of murder, death sentence for one accused, life imprisonment for the other

quotes.text: The trial court, on a consideration of the evidence, convicted both the accused for the offence punishable under Section 302 of the IPC and while Mission Suklabaidhya was awarded the death penalty, Uttam Chakraborty was ordered to undergo imprisonment for life.
We accordingly allow Criminal Appeal No. 869 of 2006, set aside his conviction and sentence and direct that he be set free forthwith, if not wanted in any other case.

neutral_facts.value: The accused-husband and his friend were friends. The accused-husband was married to a woman who was pregnant. The couple had a child who was about 4 or 5 years old. The deceased was employed as a school teacher and had engaged a domestic help who resided in their house. The prosecution alleged that the accused-husband and the domestic help had an illicit relationship, which led to frequent quarrels between the couple. On the night of the incident, the domestic help's mother was informed that her daughter had fallen ill and accompanied them to the police station. There, she learned that her daughter had died of burn injuries and lodged a FIR. During the investigation, it was found that the accused-husband was present when the deceased died. The prosecution relied primarily on the testimony of the child witness and the domestic help, as well as the post-mortem report indicating severe injuries and the removal of the foetus.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused-husband and his friend were responsible for the murder of an eight-month pregnant woman who died of burn injuries, based on the statements of PW-6, a child witness, and PW-1, the domestic help.

quotes.text: The prosecution relied primarily on the evidence of PW-6 Marjon Suklabaidhya, who was projected as an eye witness to what had happened on the fateful day, PW-1 Panchami Suklabaidya aforesaid, PW-2 the Executive Magistrate Manash Das, who held an inquest on the dead body and had noticed a huge cut injury on the person of the deceased, Radhu Paul PW-4 who stated that he had seen both the accused involved in an animated discussion in front of his shop and when he had gone close to them they had changed the topic and had started discussing some business matter and that after a short while a girl had come out and raised a hue and cry and told Mission Suklabaidhya that his wife had died of burn injuries, Nioti Rani PW-6, the mother of the deceased, who deposed to the illicit relationship of her son-in-law and PW-1, and PW-7 the doctor, Khairuz Zaman Choudhary, who had carried out the post-mortem examination and had found very severe cut injuries on the stomach which indicated that the foetus had been removed.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no substantial evidence linking the co-accused to the murder, and that the child witness's testimony was insufficient to justify a capital sentence.

quotes.text: However, notwithstanding the fact that PW-6 is a witness whose credibility has not been doubted, it would perhaps be imprudent to award a capital sentence on the statement of a child witness as observed in Suresh vs. State of UP. (1981) 2 SCC 569.
We find absolutely no evidence to connect him with the murder.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the testimony of a child witness, while potentially credible, is not sufficient to justify a capital sentence due to the inherent unreliability of such testimony.

quotes.text: Children, in the first place, mix up what they see with what they like to imagine to have seen and besides, a little tutoring is inevitable in their case in order to lend coherence and consistency to their disjointed thoughts which tend to stray. The extreme sentence cannot seek its main support from evidence of this kind which, even if true, is not safe enough to act upon for putting out a life.
